content: The prevalence of delusional disorders is estimated to be approximately 24 to 30 cases per 100,000 individuals annually. Delusional disorder accounts for about 1-2% of admissions to inpatient mental health facilities. However, the true prevalence of the disorder is likely underestimated because most individuals with delusional disorder do not perceive their condition as an illness and therefore do not seek treatment. Delusional disorders are relatively uncommon in psychiatric practice. This rarity may also be an underestimation, as individuals with the disorder often lack insight into their condition and consequently avoid psychiatric evaluation. The prevalence of delusional disorders is approximately 24 to 30 cases per 100,000 individuals annually. Females are more frequently affected by delusional disorder compared to males. Delusional disorder typically manifests in individuals during middle to late adulthood. The age range for first hospital admissions due to delusional disorder is generally between 33 and 55 years.
